name: Maize farming in Africa
summary: African farmers took up American maize, unknown on the continent in 1500 and first documented under cultivation there in 1540; it became Africa's main food crop.
description: Maize, an American crop unknown in Africa in 1500, is first documented under cultivation there in 1540, according to James McCann's history of the crop as summarised by a reviewer. It quickly became an essential food crop in the Asante kingdom, while linguistic evidence suggests that Nigerian farmers took it up later and from the north, across the Sahara, rather than from European traders on the coast. Maize is now the largest part of the national diet in sixteen African countries.

impact.note: Maize became a main food across many African societies over several centuries (reach 2) and farming and diets were reorganised around it (depth 2), with local varieties and foods as its successors (generativity 1).

date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: McCann dates the first documentary evidence of maize cultivation in Africa to 1540, as reported in a review of his book.

evidence.supports: identifying 1540 as the date for the first documentary evidence of maize cultivation in Africa

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: The 1540 date rests on a review; McCann's book should be opened for the document and the place it refers to, so that the continent-wide place can be narrowed.
Cassava in West and Central Africa, and how its processing was learned there, needs its own sources and probably its own record.
Whether maize came by the Portuguese or across the Sahara is contested; Cherniwchan and Moreno-Cruz (2019) was not opened.
The effect on population and on states such as Kongo and Asante was not checked beyond the reviewer's remarks.

research.note: The review says maize was unknown on the African continent in 1500, so it was brought from the Americas; it reports both European traders on the coast and a trans-Saharan route as carriers.
